environment.description: Same application deployed in a minimal container where the entrypoint invokes pivot_root(2) followed by chroot into /srv/sandbox prior to spawning the Node.js process. The sandbox directory tree contains only: /srv/sandbox/{app/,extracted/,tmp/uploads/,node_modules/,usr/local/bin/node,usr/local/lib/}. The process runs under a dedicated UID (65534/nobody) with no-new-privileges set. The container uses a read-only root filesystem with tmpfs mounts exclusively at /tmp and /app/extracted. An AppArmor profile (k8s-archive-svc) denies write to any path not matching /app/extracted/** or /tmp/uploads/**. The combination means even if path traversal resolves to e.g. /../../../etc/passwd, the chroot boundary maps that to /srv/sandbox/etc/passwd which doesn't exist, and the AppArmor write denial prevents creating files outside the two allowed path prefixes regardless of traversal.

config.sensitive_files_in_sandbox: none - no /etc/shadow, no credentials, no service tokens
